name: Debug Interface Exploitation
description: Identification, access, and exploitation of hardware debug interfaces including JTAG, SWD, UART, and vendor-specific debug ports. Covers physical identification of test points, protocol enumeration, authentication bypass, and leveraging debug access for memory extraction, code execution, and device compromise.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to hardware debug interfaces

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands common debug protocols and their security implications
evidence: Can explain JTAG, SWD, and UART protocols at a conceptual level
Understands why debug interfaces are a security risk in production devices
Familiar with common debug adapter hardware (J-Link, ST-Link, Bus Pirate)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Connects to and interacts with identified debug interfaces under supervision
evidence: Successfully connects to a UART console and interacts with a bootloader
Uses OpenOCD to connect to a JTAG/SWD target with known pinout
Dumps memory contents via debug interface with documented procedures
Identifies debug headers and test points on a PCB with guidance

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently identifies and exploits debug interfaces on unfamiliar targets
evidence: Identifies JTAG/SWD pinouts on unpopulated headers using JTAGulator or manual probing
Bypasses basic debug authentication (e.g., JTAG lock bits via voltage glitch)
Extracts full memory contents and achieves code execution via debug interfaces
Completes debug interface assessments on 3+ distinct hardware platforms independently

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Exploits protected debug interfaces; develops custom debug tooling; mentors team
evidence: Bypasses vendor-specific debug authentication mechanisms
Develops custom OpenOCD configurations and debug scripts for novel targets
Exploits vendor-specific boot ROM download/recovery modes (e.g., MediaTek BROM, Qualcomm EDL)
Mentors junior analysts on debug interface identification and exploitation
Contributes to lab methodology for debug interface assessment

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Recognized authority on debug interface security; publishes novel bypass techniques
evidence: Discovered and published novel debug authentication bypass techniques
Develops lab training program for debug interface exploitation
Provides expert consultation on debug interface hardening to silicon vendors
Authored CVEs or research papers on debug interface vulnerabilities

assessment_methods.description: Identify and exploit debug interfaces on a prepared target with no prior documentation
Observe the analyst's physical probing technique, signal identification, and tool usage during a live assessment

equipment: Bus Pirate or equivalent multi-protocol interface
